visualReview.notes: Inspected eight portable views. All four radial sectors and recessed approach positions read from above. Street views distinguish two glazed rings, the opaque tier and the saddle auditorium roof. The east and west ramps meet the modeled approach grade.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected eight dated shared-surface views. Pale structural concrete, board-formed concrete, dark glazing and metal roof are visibly distinct. The exact four-sector footprint is evident in plan and the dated placement unload passed.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected 24 current detail, context and transition views. All four levels preserve the four wings, ramps, rings and saddle. Closer levels add terrace rails, upper fins, glazing divisions and door frames.

geographicReview.notes: Registered to the original 46-corner mapped theatre way. The original 256-meter elevation field is preserved. The four ramps terminate on the sampled forecourt and the building-specific mask is limited to the dated generic structure.

fidelityReview.scope: The April 1978 exterior of the National Arts Theatre in Iganmu, Lagos. Includes the four radial gallery sectors, ramped entrances, glazed roof-terrace rings and distinctive saddle shell over the main auditorium. The modern station, campus additions, interiors and surrounding grounds are outside the model.
fidelityReview.notes: The original mapped envelope fixes the four radial sectors. The written field report supplies the four ramped entrances, three terrace rings, two glazed tiers and the tensioned saddle shell. The published 31-meter height anchors the section. The April 1978 ramp lengths, window placement, shell shape and finishes are estimates.

imageryReview.notes: The exact cleared Qualla photograph records the 1978 visit from inside. No exterior architecture is visible. The dated exterior uses mapped geometry and written records without adopting source imagery.

primaryFactsReview.notes: The original named footprint establishes the four radial sectors. Written sources supply the approximate overall height, saddle shell and rings. The only cleared Qualla photograph is an interior event view.

limitations: The original modern mapped building footprint and its four radial sectors establish the structure. The section is reconstructed from the documented 31-meter height, four ramped entrances, three roof-terrace rings, two glazed tiers and a saddle shell. The 1978 façade proportions, roof curvature and finishes are visual estimates.

The provider heightfield is preserved and includes probable influence from roofs or vegetation. It does not establish the 1978 forecourt survey grade. Foundations and ramps use approximate registration. The individual approach positions, thresholds and ramp lengths estimate grade from samples around the mapped footprint.
The model depicts the April 1978 exterior. Later station and renovated campus features, interiors and adjacent grounds are outside scope.
